content.what_it_is: Fixed-form Fortran main program that reads grid dimensions, spacing, channel depth/width, and bank slope from bathy_param.txt (L6-L16), allocates depth and coordinate matrices (L18), initializes a constant-depth channel and coordinates (L20-L26), reduces depth linearly outside half the channel width (L28-L35), and writes one formatted depth row per J to depth.txt (L37-L42).

equations.ref: bank depth starts at channel depth minus slope distance

unresolved: The y-coordinate formula L24 is not cell-centered symmetrically for even Nglob: it yields indices from `(1-Nglob/2)*DY` through `(Nglob/2)*DY` (for Nglob=100, -49*DY through +50*DY). Because bank depth uses abs(Y) at L30-L32, the two sides contain unequal coordinate extents and can receive asymmetric depth values despite symmetric input parameters.

The output format has exactly 9000 F descriptors at L41 while the implied-DO writes Mglob values at L39. If Mglob exceeds 9000, Fortran format reversion can continue the same J values on another record, breaking the intended one-grid-row-per-record layout.
No bounds/physical validation prevents nonpositive Mglob/Nglob/DX/DY, negative width, or slopes large enough to make DEPTH negative outside the channel (L9-L35).
OPEN/READ/ALLOCATE/WRITE have no IOSTAT or size checks, so missing/malformed input and allocation/output failures are uncontrolled.
